_comment: THE PIN: which commit of legalese/canon the vendored mirror under
jl4/examples/canon/ is a copy of, and which of its directories are blessed
as part of this repository's regression corpus.
Ruled 2026-09-15 by Meng; the ruling is quoted verbatim in
specs/todo/CANON-REGRESSION-CORPUS-SPEC.md §1. jl4/examples/legal/ IS the
language's regression corpus and stays one; these canon directories join
it; a subject already in canon leaves l4-ide (moved, not lost); the rest
stay where they are.
DO NOT EDIT THE MIRROR. Edit in canon, then `etc/sync-canon.mjs --bump
<sha>`. CI runs `--check` on every PR and fails when the mirror and canon
disagree, which is what makes this DETECTED duplication rather than the
silent kind.
--- the SHA is on a person's shelf, and that is still a known compromise ---
SPEC §3B.6 says a blessed dir 'lives on canon main'. This pin does not:
the `sha` below is on `mengwong/drafts` — see `ref` — because that is where
the content is. The target is canon `main`; re-pin there when these
directories reach it, and delete this paragraph rather than softening it.
(This paragraph used to name the SHA a second time, in prose. It went stale
on the very next bump, because a sha written twice is a sha that can
disagree with itself. `sha` and `ref` below are the single copy.)
A shelf SHA can be rebased away. If it is, `--pull` fails to fetch it — the
failure is loud, which is the property being relied on.
`pinned` IS A UTC DATE, written by `writePin` from `toISOString()`, and it
will therefore read one day EARLIER than the local date whenever a bump
lands after 08:00 SGT. That is not staleness. bb675a98 was committed
2026-09-15 beside prose dated the 16th. This has now been filed as a defect
once and refuted once; the note is cheaper than the next round trip.
HISTORY, retired 2026-09-16: this pin briefly pointed at a canon BRANCH
(`gm/rebless-2026-09-15`, then `gm/canon-fixture-2026-09-16`) because the
first run of this mechanism found a stale golden and re-blessing it needed a
canon commit before drafts had one. Both are merged into drafts now, so the
pin points at the shelf itself and the branch-vs-shelf reasoning no longer
applies. What it taught is worth keeping: canon has merge, squash AND rebase
all enabled, so a squash or rebase merge mints a NEW sha and leaves the
original reachable only from its branch — `delete_branch_on_merge` being
false is what saves such a pin. Pin a shelf or a main SHA in preference to a
branch SHA for exactly that reason.
sg/succession/encodings/cleanroom-2026-08 — two of its files
(family-cases.l4, probate-administration-act.l4) exit non-zero from
`l4 check` on today's binary, on an Info-level diagnostic at
daydate.l4:104:8-104:50, WHILE THEIR COMMITTED GOLDENS SAY 'Evaluation
successful'. The goldens were blessed by an older binary. That is exactly
the drift this mechanism exists to make visible, so the directory stays out
until its goldens are re-blessed in canon.
sg/pdpa-2012 — no goldens at all. A directory with no goldens cannot be a
regression corpus; `failFirstTime` would write them on the first run and
pass on the second, which tests the harness and not the compiler.
il/ofek-hadash-2008 WAS excluded on that same ground and no longer is:
canon e29c69a3 blessed its 36 goldens (nine modules, four each), so it is
in the blessed list below as of 2026-09-19. Read that commit before
trusting them — it records WHICH BINARY wrote them and why the timing
mattered. They were generated from unstable at ec20584c1, after four PRs
that move golden bytes landed on 2026-09-18: #419 (schema goldens double-
encoded every non-ASCII character, smucclaw#962), #415 (nlg escapes), #418
(\> in @ref, which also routes unescapeNlgText through the text/html/json/
AKN export path) and #423 (@nlg:xx language tags). #419 is the one that
bites this encoding: 524 of its lines carry non-ASCII, so goldens blessed a
day earlier would have been wrong in all nine schema files. That is the
general rule this row is evidence for — a canon directory is blessable the
day its goldens come from a binary at the tree they will be checked
against, not the day someone wants it in the corpus.
One caveat that blessing does NOT dispose of: ofek-pay.nlg.golden is empty,
because that module carries no directive to linearise. It is an accurate
record of an empty population and a test that cannot fail. It is left as
measured rather than dropped, because a missing golden and an empty one say
different things and only one of them is true here.
--- the flattening, which is the one place the mirror is not verbatim ----
Two blessed directories keep a cases file one level down, in `cases/`,
while its goldens sit in the directory-level `tests/`. jl4/tests/Main.hs
derives a golden's path as `takeDirectory inputFile </> "tests"`, so a
file at `cases/x.l4` is looked up at `cases/tests/x.golden` — and canon has
no `cases/tests/` directory anywhere (measured at this pin). The mirror
therefore HOISTS `cases/*.l4` to the directory root, which is the only
layout in which canon's own goldens are the ones the harness reads.
sync-canon.mjs applies the same rule in both directions, so `--check` is
not fooled by it, and refuses on a name collision rather than overwriting.
_rebless: FIRST PIN BUMP, 2026-09-15, and what caused it: the first harness run over
the mirror failed on canon/sg/child-support/sg-csp.l4 (1 of 90). Canon's
tests/sg-csp.golden was two lines; today's binary adds a 19-line Info block
at sg-csp.l4:79:8 — the ASSUME-retirement diagnostic. THE BINARY IS RIGHT:
that diagnostic is landed behaviour, and l4-ide's own corpus was swept for
it in #337 while canon's was not. The golden was re-blessed in canon on
branch gm/rebless-2026-09-15 (parent 299dd490) and the pin moved here.
The mirror was NOT hand-edited — doing that would have made this repo's copy
disagree with canon silently, which is the failure the pin exists to prevent.
Canon's sg-csp.l4:79 still USES ASSUME; the diagnostic is telling its author
to move to a section-level GIVEN. Re-blessing makes the golden truthful.
Migrating the encoding is a canon-side improvement and is not done.
SECOND RE-BLESS, 2026-09-19, canon 5ef8f9cb — and it was found from a
DIFFERENT directory, which is the part worth keeping. Blessing
il/ofek-hadash-2008 required moving the pin past canon 02fad47, and that
commit had brought seven sg/penal-code-1871 schema goldens carrying a
double-encoded em-dash: the byte run c3a2 c280 c294, each byte of the
correct e2 80 94 re-encoded as UTF-8 in its own right. They were blessed on
2026-09-17; l4-ide #419 (smucclaw#962) fixed exactly that and merged
2026-09-18 12:49Z. A day's gap, and the goldens were on the wrong side of it.
THE MEASUREMENT THAT LICENSED THE FIX: decoding each committed golden's
mojibake yields the current output BYTE FOR BYTE, so the whole diff is the
encoding. The three penal-code schema goldens NOT touched are the three
whose output is pure ASCII — the bug had nothing to mangle in them. That
split is the control: a non-ASCII golden coming back identical, or an ASCII
one moving, would have meant something other than the encoding fix.
THE GENERAL LESSON, which cost a false negative to learn. The staleness was
LATENT, not live: at the previous pin this directory had one schema golden
and it was clean, so l4-ide was green and would have gone red on the next
bump by anyone, for a reason belonging to neither of the two changes
involved. A pin bump is therefore not only 'does MY directory pass' — it
adopts every blessed directory's drift since the last bump, so run the FULL
suite before committing one. And the first attempt to screen for this
grepped for the GLYPHS 'Â' and 'â€' and reported all directories clean,
which was wrong: the double-encoded em-dash's middle byte is an invisible
control character. Grep the BYTES (xxd -p | grep c3a2c280c294), never the
rendering.
